source_row.stem: A nurse is caring for a client with negative pressure wound therapy, or wound VAC, and a family member assumes this device probably just delivers antibiotic medication directly into the wound. This therapy instead works by:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Applying positive rather than negative pressure to the wound bed to encourage new tissue growth, which reverses the actual mechanism this therapy uses","B":"Simply sealing the wound without any active suction or pressure-based mechanism involved, contrary to the active mechanism this therapy actually uses","C":"Delivering topical antibiotic medication directly into the wound bed as its primary mechanism, similar to what the family member is currently assuming this device does","D":"Applying controlled negative pressure to the wound, promoting granulation tissue formation and removing exudate, rather than delivering antibiotics as the family member is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: Negative pressure wound therapy applies controlled negative (vacuum) pressure to the wound bed, promoting granulation tissue formation, improving blood flow, and removing excess exudate.
source_row.source_name: FDA — Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Overview
